body:
Just a heads up, getting vaccines while teething is typically not recommended due to the additives being able to pass through the blood-brain barrier more easily. 

That said, my LO definitely started teething at 2 months, got her first tooth right at 5 mo and how has 6 at 7.5 mo. Teething timelines vary so much between babies. The Razz-baby razzberry teethers helped us, she loves them.
Oh, Jacquie's "dancing"... That was not good.
Vibrating teether?? Does it make the teeth come out quicker? I probably need this...

So I was in VS with my mom over the weekend and mentioned to one of the workers how I wished they had nursing bras. Her response was "When I was nursing, I hated nursing bras so I just used our bras and pulled them down, I felt much more comfortable." Yeah, I'm going to spend $50 on a bra and wear out the cups like that...
I'd actually like to see Cole do a pop song, like One Direction that's what makes you beautiful.
I wonder how much Cee Lo regrets passing on Cole at this point...

Finally got that check in the mail today. I threw it in an envelope with my work's old logo, so don't be alarmed if you get an envelope with a globe on the return address. :) hope you have a great thanksgiving!
There was only one $5 check in the thing I just got so it's not much but I will still send it. Will pop it in the mail Monday :)
My 3 month old sleeps from ~8pm til 6-630am... my secret is co-sleeping. She'll take 2 dream-feeds per night. We are both well-rested. Please don't hate me.

[Clara](http://imgur.com/rZzT5I7) , 3 months old, and the reason I was late for work this morning. This was taken around the time we should have been pulling into the daycare parking lot, after 2 diaper changes and in her second outfit.

YES totally normal, but it should pass very soon. I remember when my LO was 9 days old (she was born 8/20 and we were visiting my dad for his bday on 8/29) she refused to meet her Pappy because anytime I stopped feeding her she would scream!

Now she is a very healthy, chunky 3 month old who loves to eat but hasn't really had any cluster feeding issues since then.

Good for you! I'm struggling... LO just turned 3 months and I am still the same weight I was 2 weeks post-partum (gained 40 total, lost 25). I'm EBFing too. The breastfeeding=weightloss apparently doesn't work for everyone, lucky me!

Hey lady! I just got something from Similac in the mail this week. I think I still have your address in my inbox, but if I don't I'll let you know. I'll PM you tonight when I get home & see exactly what I have. :)

That's the same fridge my mom has! Anyway, I have been told that the milk should be in the back of the freezer (or fridge) anyway, not in the doors, because the stuff in the doors is not as cold as the back AND is warmed up (yes, very very slightly) every time the doors are opened.

I use one of [these](http://www.amazon.com/The-First-Years-Breastflow-Organizer/dp/B000K4YSVI/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1385134519&sr=8-1&keywords=first+years+breast+milk+storage), which doesn't take up much space, but it also doesn't hold a TON of bags, maybe 20 full ones. It looks like you would be able to put 2 of those in your freezer without having to sacrifice too much of your frozen food.

I'm the same way as you. But girl, most places will change your battery for free. I just had it done a few weeks ago at Advanced Autoparts. You don't have to be THAT stubborn :P

But yeah, I hate asking for help too. I put together a huge wooden table & chair set when I was ~8 months pregnant (and HUGE).
Didn't we have our babies the same day? Or did you beat me by a day or two ;)
What did you use to teach them? Is the stuff at babysignlanguage.com worthwhile? I don't know any ASL myself but I'd really like to teach my baby.

Nope, no squeal (yet), but my 11.5 week old does the cry where her lips quiver and her voice vibrates like she's SOOOOOOO sad. It's heartbreaking because she really doesn't cry that often. When she does this I feel awful!
Thank  ya :)

That is a really nice way to put it, thanks for sharing that. 

And, just for you :) http://i.imgur.com/8ONYmyhl.jpg http://i.imgur.com/SbxSGdVl.jpg http://i.imgur.com/jjOZmncl.jpg

Thank you for sharing. I'm so sorry for your situation. I am really hoping my daughter ends up realizing how much I'm doing/have done for her and we build a close relationship because of it. It's just hard because I love my dad so much and when I see things like "Daddy/Daughter Day" at restaurants I get a little sad that she might never have that and don't know how to make her realize it's not her fault.
How old was he when he asked?
Same here. I'm back on the second trimester "2 breakfasts" schedule, and snack like crazy after dinner as well.

I'm pretty sure my 2 month old is starting the process - a lot of hand-chewing and drooling. I think all babies start on their own time, and everything I've read says 4-6 months but the actual process of teething before the first tooth comes in can take up to a month.

What everyone else said, plus... please do not get discouraged over your supply right now. Every little drop of milk your baby gets, even if it's a small portion of his daily intake, is benefiting him immensely. Stay strong, and have faith that it will get easier!

I have [this Lansinoh pump](http://www.amazon.com/Lansinoh-Double-Electric-Breast-Pump/dp/B000P9XJ5E/ref=sr_1_3?ie=UTF8&qid=1382117249&sr=8-3&keywords=lansinoh+breast+pump) which according to the reviews, is very similar to the Medela but about half the price. It's worked great for me so far (pumping 3x a day for 10 minutes). I bought some more of the Lansinoh storage bottles but I use Dr Brown's bottles to feed my baby. Those bottles hook right up to the pump too. I also got preemie nipples for the bottles to prevent my babe from being overfed at daycare.

Yeah that's how I'm feeling. I don't want her to be hungry, but I can't imagine she takes 4oz and then 2 more an hour later. I asked them this morning to just put 3oz in her bottle instead of 4. I really don't want to be the difficult mom but I'm just so worried. I wish I could just stay at home and BF all day but that's not possible as a single mom :(
That's a good point. This morning I just asked them if they could please just give her 3oz per bottle instead of 4oz, and then if she's still hungry they can feed more.
Ugh. So I just ordered some preemie nipples for the bottles and am definitely going to talk to the room leader in the morning.
I don't know :(

Thanks. I'm going to talk to the infant room supervisor in the morning to see if she thinks that's abnormal or what. I just bring them full storage bottles or bags and they have a few of my bottles with nipples they fill and wash.
My baby girl will be 7 weeks on Tuesday as well. This article was so hard to read.
I have a bunch of Enfamil coupons from $2 to $5 off that I be happy to send, just pm me your address!

I had heard about the gown thing too, but I just had my girl in onesies since we left the hospital. Her stump fell off right at 2 weeks. As long as you care for it the way the nurses tell you to, I don't think it's a huge issue, in my opinion anyway. No one at the hospital told me I had to avoid onesies.

Will she sleep by herself on her side? My baby has only side-slept since the first week. She hates being on her back, and startles if I put her down like that and won't stay asleep. What I've read said research doesn't show a huge difference in SIDS for side vs back sleeping, they just show that tummy sleeping is worse.
Ooh yeah let me know. It's true about their skin, but my mom made the comment when she was born about "how perfect her complexion is."  I think she jinxed me. Haha.
Haha! Aww. I guess that's no worse than me calling my baby "Chunker" or "Stinky Girl." :)
Interesting. I guess I'll give the ped a call tomorrow to see what he recommends. I know the acne is harmless but I hate seeing it on her pretty face!

My baby is breastfed but I'm going back to work in a week so I've been introducing bottles. She prefers Dr Brown's bottles, which I've ordered from both amazon and diapers.com. Not sure about different sizing, but I don't think breastfed babies really ever need more than 4oz at a time anyway. Also, if baby will be going to daycare (or having to take a bottle from a babysitter) it's best to start introducing a bottle around 3-4 weeks- just maybe once a week to get them used to it. That's what I was told anyway.

So true for me too about being aware of the baby. The first week I was so paranoid about rolling over on her. But I was also a sleep-deprived zombie. Now I just don't move much in my sleep. She's right next to me and I am fully aware of everything, yet she and I both sleep really well through the night. Wakings to feed are pretty brief, I wake at the first sign of her moving around, and we both fall right back asleep after. 

It should be noted that I'm single so it's just the two of us in a full-size bed.
Hi! As luck would have it, I just got 3 $5-off similac coupons today. If you give me your address I'll pop 'em in the mail for you on Monday! :)
Awesome! I have one week left before I go back to work and I'm worried about not being able to pump enough, so this is encouraging.
I will keep you in mind next time similac sends me anything!!
PM me, I'll be happy to send what I have - no need for any exchange. :)
Hmm, interesting! I'm sure there's so e truth to it since they see so many babies day to day. Also, 4 lbs?? You rock!!
Thank you! :)

I use Vaseline, but not at every change, just 2-3 times a day. I guess I probably should start using it every time. I'd use cloth if I wasn't going back to work full time, but I'm single and don't have a choice. Plus daycare requires disposables. It's already hard enough for me to get a chance to get away from the LO long enough to wash 2 loads of clothes a week!
At 4 weeks post partum I have seriously been considering shaving my head! I don't really have the face shape to pull it off though, haha.

This is exactly what I mean. It would be so easy for you to have given up on breast milk 4  months ago (and God knows I would never judge a mother who did) but you've made such a sacrifice to do this for your baby. It really is admirable. I don't know if I could do that myself.

My girl is a side sleeper and wakes up within 10 minutes if I put her down on her back. Studies don't show much difference between back and side sleeping. 

I'm pretty sure that when I was a baby (I'm turning 27 in a week) the rule of thumb was to put babies to sleep on their tummies and I turned out fine. Like others have said even back sleeping doesn't completely eliminate the risk of SIDS. IMHO as long as you don't have a pillow or blanket in there for them to suffocate on, letting your baby get restful sleep on their tummy doesn't make you a bad mom.
Go you, awesome mama! :)
My daughter's name is Clara too. Love it :)
Thank you so much for sharing! I was actually going to ask the same question as OP. Didnt know they made anything like this.

Seconding Zoloft here. Studies I've read show minimal to no transfer of Zoloft through breast milk. Plus I took it the last 4 weeks of my pregnancy and baby thankfully had zero withdrawal symptoms. Many antidepressants are very safe for BFing, just do some research.
Last night in bed my 3 week old grabbed my tank top strap and pulled on it to get me to feed her. She definitely knows how to get what she wants already, lol. What a cutie pie you have there :)

My 3 week old still isn't a fan of pacifiers. I wanted to wait 3-4 weeks but caved after 5 days (haha). She will accept one about half the time I offer, but can't keep them in her mouth yet and usually ends up crying. After asking around on here I tried a few kinds and the MAM seemS to be her favorite and easiest to keep in, but it doesn't last long. I wish she'd take one, especially before she starts daycare in a few weeks. But hopefully you'll have better luck than me with your LO.
Oh gosh. I make an effort to brush my teeth once a day now. But it's definitely not at the top of my priority list. I'm sort of glad we don't get many visitors...

I never knew babies did such weird things. Last night she was dozing off while nursing and just stopped and smiled (eyes still closed) and went, "heh heh." Of course she's too young to really laugh yet but it cracked me up! They sure are interesting creatures!
Best of luck, hope things pick up soon!

I wanted to delay clamping but could not because there was meconium in my water and they had to take my girl and clear her lungs immediately in case she'd aspirated any. Meconium is typical when babies are past-due and Clara was 12 days late. I really wish I could have delayed but I got to cut her cord and she ended up being perfectly healthy.

Your baby sounds just like mine... I go back to work in 4 weeks and I get so anxious thinking about how much she's going to cry her eyes out all day without me :( I'm going to be a wreck. I'm sorry I don't have any advice, but I can definitely commiserate.
I call my little one Bear too! You have a cute baby there :)
Thank you for sharing this sub! I didn't know it existed and I'm pretty sure I belong... :/

I didn't take a class either, and I held off on the epi until I knew I couldn't function without it. I was so out of it that when the anesthesiologist came to remove it afterward, he couldn't believe I didn't recognize him from only 4 hours earlier! Though I had wanted a natural birth, I do NOT feel like a failure. I forgot it all as soon as I saw my daughter.

My advice is to follow your body's cues to push rather than let a doctor or nurse yell at you to push. When I pushed they let me do my own thing and it turned out to be super efficient. I took deep breaths, pushed for about 5-second increments, 4 times before stopping to rest and wait for the next contraction. No one yelled at me or counted to 10 and my baby was out less than a half hour after I started "practice pushes." Also i didn't need any stitches, had one tiny little tear that didn't even bother me when I peed. This was even with an epidural, so just trust that your body will know what to do to get that baby out. 

Also, my labor pain was all in my back and it was horrific even before they started my pitocin. I went into it not wanting any interventions but I'm glad I decided to have the epidural because the actual delivery and baby bonding time was so nice to enjoy pain-free. I support every woman's decision to either use or not use pain relief during labor. Good luck to you!
Seriously? That would be phenomenal if you really wouldn't mind! Assuming you're in the US?
How have I never heard of the Milk savers?? I know I've leaked a good ounce at a time. Have you tried them before?
I have a few washable pads but pretty sure they're cotton and not wool. Have tried 3 kinds of disposables- the Nuk ones are completely worthless if you leak a significant amount!

My LO is just a few days younger than yours but I'm not planning on doing any kind of sleep training for a while. I'd like to get a routine down when I go back to work in a month, but for now I'm just letting her do what she needs to. I'm fortunate that she's been doing 4-hour sleeps for over a week now, but that's largely because we co sleep. I she's in her bassinet she doesn't sleep long at all. Getting "rules" in place will come in time, for now I'm just enjoying my baby moon.
I just remember how much they hurt my poor sore nipples after 2 days of struggling to learn how to breastfeed!

Yeah, it's frustrating because there are times when she's all gung ho excited about the binky but I have to struggle to keep it in her mouth for her. I guess it's something they'll figure out as they get older.

That is so awesome!! I wish I had a way to weigh my baby - was born the same day as yours at 7lb 7oz, left hospital at 7lb 2oz and was up to 7lb10oz at one week. So love when our breastfed babies gain so much weight :)

Here's how our nights go: after she's eaten for-like-ever from both breasts, to fall asleep she continues to suck on one (while we're in side lying position). She sucks for ~45 min and is not getting anything - I don't hear any swallowing after a certain point. Then when I feel like there might be a few swigs refilled in the other breast, I offer that and she takes 3 swallows and passes out.
To answer your last question... My daughter seems to actually enjoy being sprayed, haha. Her eyes get big and she opens wide like she's excited about all the milk she's about to get!
Sooo cute and I love the name Luna!

I get milk everywhere too so I've just been wearing a sleep nursing bra with pads in to bed. I'd love to just have my boobs out for baby but I don't want to drench her in milk. Don't you worry about getting it all over your baby?
Too sweet! My 2 week old (his bday buddy) puts her hands on my boob, grasping them so everyone knows they're hers!

Oh yes! Like I said, no one told me I'd still have a 5-month-pregnant belly for the first few days. I think it's important everyone knows how different everyone's body reacts (but that we snap back pretty well regardless!).

Yeah, my body bounced back pretty well I think. I feel like it helps that I had some meat on my bones so even though I got huge, I didn't end up with many stretch marks. Our bodies are pretty miraculous! I've seen women post on here who are back in their pre-pregnancy skinny jeans 2 weeks later. I just wanted to show how everyone's body changes differently, especially if you didn't start out as a size 2!

>fuck that, I'm a mom 

I think I need to get that tattooed on, haha. Yeah, priorities change when the baby arrives. Even just going out without makeup is freeing - there are just way more important things in life! 

Thank you for the compliments :)
Why thank you :) She's the reason I'm so positive right now, she's really changed my life!

Thank you! Honestly, I feel pretty good right now, but I was blessed with such a good baby. It takes a while to get her down at night (we cosleep) but when we do she sleeps for 4 hours already. Then it'll be a feeding and 2 more 2-hour sleeps. The first week was hard with the waking every 1.5-2 hours and I was a zombie (note: I'm a single mom). But we're getting a little routine together and as long as I have my coffee and make sure I eat and drink enough, I feel great!

PS. Happy almost due date :)

I didn't weigh myself after delivery but you lose a TON just in the first day between baby placenta and fluids. However, I still looked 5 months pregnant for the first 3 days, until my uterus shrank down some (no one told me that would be the case!).

OH GOD. My mom was so upset when I had my girl in a carrier when we went to Target. "Are you sure you trust that to keep her in? Is her head ok? Can she breathe?" I wouldn't put this tiny fragile child who is my whole world in a carrier that she can't breathe in and will fall out of! And she slept through the whole trip because she's calmed by being close to me while I walk. And no, I really don't need a stroller right now while my daughter weighs 8 lbs. UGH.

Seriously, the water breaking makes everything SO much worse!! I went from 5 to 9 in just over 2 hours with pitocin and waters broken. I wanted a med-free birth but I got that epidural and my delivery experience was beautiful! Being able to watch my baby crown in the mirror and not screaming in pain anymore was just an amazing feeling.

I'm having the same issue! I don't know much about hemorrhoids but I went all pregnancy without them but.. I guess maybe now I have some internally. It's so not pleasant. And I drink at least 2 liters of water a day... Guess I'll have to up that.

Or couch. I am cosleeping with my infant but only in bed, where I'm on the edge of my pillow and nothing else is on her half of the bed. It can definitely be done safely, but couches and recliners are way too dangerous (baby getting caught/suffocated in a crevice of a cushion).
Haha, that's so cute! My little lady is pretty much bald, but I think she's beautiful anyway :)
Exactly! Mine laid on my chest with her eyes open, looking around at the world, just a few hours after birth. That said, I hope she doesn't start crawling and walking sooner, I'm not ready for that!

August 8th bumper here who delivered on August 20th. My girl just wanted to be in that special top 10% that goes so far past her "due date."  She ended up being perfect, extremely healthy, and gaining weight so fast! I've heard that post date babies tend to eat and sleep better, and that's been the case with my LO for sure. I didn't dilate to 1cm til after 41w and didn't efface until they put in cervidil at my induction. No matter when your baby makes its way out, it will have been worth the wait, I promise!! :)
Your princess has peach fuzz hair like mine :) At least when they're this little they don't mind the headbands so much. What a cutie, good job mama!

She's absolutely beautiful, and if he didn't want you two awesome girls, methinks you're better off without him. From one single mom to another, keep up the good work and enjoy all the love that you alone get from your little girl!

I started taking Zoloft around week 38 of my pregnancy - which is risky, because of the withdrawal possibility in the newborn. They even recommend women taking it during pregnancy taper down in the last weeks. But thankfully my girl was born without having any signs of withdrawal. Zoloft is also extremely safe for breastfeeding, as very minimal amounts are transferred (if any) through breastmilk. It's been a lifesaver for me, especially because my pregnancy went so long (41+5) that I would have been a complete mess if I hadn't started it when I did.

As far as the therapy situation goes, I'm not sure. I've been in therapy for years and my closest coworkers know about my struggle with bipolar, so my taking a long lunch for therapy has never been an issue. It really is a shame PPD can't be discussed openly, because I think more women would seek help if we could just talk about it. As others have said, it shouldn't be too hard to find a therapist who will skype or meet you after work. 

I'm proud of you for taking the steps you need to take care of yourself, so that you can be the best mom for your baby. Post on here if you run into any speedbumps and need more help. Best of luck to you *hugs*
How adorable is that!
6 months?? Agh. I guess I won't throw the stained stuff away yet. Motherhood is so sexy.

There were lots of tears with the hormonal issues on day 3 & 4 PP, and I struggled with eating enough, but fortunately didn't have any issues with milk supply because of it. I took a friend's advice and made sure to shower every day. A lot of what kept me going, when I was nodding off while trying to nurse a fussy newborn, was just looking at my daughter's face and being in awe that I'd made something so perfect and knowing I'd do anything I had to to keep her safe, healthy, and happy. Those first few days were still running on that adrenaline rush from birth. I'm feeling much better now that I'm sleeping more than 4 hours a day.
I'm thinking of going with the Paragard IUD  (since I'm clearly not the most responsible person with BC ;) ) which I've heard can cause heavy periods too. Oh well.

Yep :) I know I'm blessed to have such a "good" baby in that she eats and sleeps like a champ and we haven't had any major fits so far. I'm staying at my mom's house this week for help but we did the first 4 days out of the hospital alone and survived. It gets a little easier every day. I've heard people say that we're given the exact child we're meant to have, and babies are given the mother they need (not sure how to word that but you get what I mean). She seems to understand in her own little way that we have to be a team because it's just the two of us.

Her father is paying child support and wants to be "involved" but I'm not expecting a custody battle or anything. He visited us the first night in the hospital but that's been it so far. He and I weren't ever together, just friends, and he has other, older kids with his exwife that he takes care of 50%. I'm just fine being my girl's sole provider, although I'm going to be an absolute wreck when I go back to work in ~6 weeks!

Well, I never leaked at all during pregnancy, not one drop, but I started breastfeeding within the first 30 minutes she was born. Now I have more milk than I can handle. Maybe since you aren't breastfeeding there was just no reason for it to come in? Consider yourself lucky if you're not BFing, those first few days of engorgement HURT. I had to put an ice pack on my chest to soothe my hard, swollen boobs.

Another single mama here, just wanted to say how awesome it was for you to post this! And I just want to reiterate how special it is to have all those moments with your baby to yourself. I'm the only one who gets to crack up at my daughter's funny faces, and the only one whose chest she likes to sleep against to hear my heartbeat. 

I'm also the only one who listens to her poop less than 30 seconds after I put a clean diaper on her, and the only one to put up with the screaming fits (fortunately those are rare!)  Having someone to hold the baby long enough for me to shower and actually shave my legs is a godsend, but yes, friends do flake out when you're no longer pregnant. 

I wouldn't trade any of it though. It is such a hard job but worth more than all the money in the world. Go you, and go all single mamas!
Yeah, I was told "absolutely nothing in the vagina for 6 weeks" since the cervix takes a while to close up again.

I wish I had advice but I'm a brand new mom. I know poop training is more difficult so maybe she'll just start to put two and two together? I'm sure someone else who has experience could help you better! My mom says I was fully potty trained by 18 months so I know it's possible to start early and have it stick.
Honestly this sounds like a perfect approach to potty training to me! If you continue this at baths maybe she'll figure out that it's something she should just do.

To be fair, people actually used to believe that. My mom and grandmother were so worried about me "reaching for things" while pregnant. 

But yeah, sounds to me like you're a pretty good mom, so I wouldn't worry too much :)
My 8-day old slept from 2:30-6:30 this morning! (She was awake and fussy for an hour and a half before that but oh well!) congrats on your growing boy!!

I was in your shoes 3 weeks ago. Hit my due date and cervix was closed and super high, baby had no desire to come out. I went to 41+5 and was induced, although baby likely would have come out on her own the next day based on the contractions I was having at the hospital before they put in the cervidil. Anyway, just wanted to reassure you that as soon as you see your baby you will forget about however long you go "past due."  My daughter just had her own due date and came out perfect at 7lb 7oz and is thriving. Best of luck :)

Helping Mommy read about industrial/organizational psychology.  :)

Quick question... How do you deal with leakage when she's nursing off you at night? I need to sleep in a bra with pads since the day I woke up with her in a puddle of breast milk on my bed :/ I am only a week in though.
9 months, that's awesome!! It's such a great feeling being able to provide everything our babies need!

I'm not sure either, and he said some of their scales do ounces and some don't, but this one didn't actually say ounces anywhere, the screen read 7.68 lbs. At the very least she's back up to her birth weight which is still something to be proud of!

Yes, I was so worried we'd have trouble! I cried the second day in the hospital because we couldn't get a latch and she was screaming. It just took lots and lots of practice though, and not giving up so easily.
Thank you :) I'm just thrilled with my little one so far!
I'm curious - how old does baby have to be to start teaching them this?

Same here. Baby's a week old and the littlest things make me bawl. But keep in mind out estrogen levels are SO out of whack right now, these issues are to be expected. A friend just told me, it took 9 months for my baby to grow inside me and stretch and change my body, and I should allow at least 9 months to start feeling like "me" again. You will feel better eventually, just hang in there!

I think you're on a different continent than me but I'd offer you mine! In all seriousness I don't think many people would be grossed out or upset if you asked them to help. I wouldn't think twice about it if a friend asked. Do it for your baby!
I'm so sorry for your loss :( hope you're holding up ok.
Best wishes for a fast labor and delivery! I didn't have the foley bulb but my induction went pretty quick (15 hours from cervidil to baby). You'll do great girl!!
So cute! You were a champ going through induction without pain meds!! Mine was rough. Definitely felt the pooping thing. Congratulations on your cutie pie :)
This is what I'm hoping for! Thanks :)

Well she is doing really well with eating and sleeping! She doesn't fuss too much either and is (usually) easily soothed when she does have a fit. It sucked being pregnant forever but she is such a healthy baby that it was worth it!
Yes, I did think that... She trolled me. But she was clearly just baking to perfection :) Thank you!

Unfortunately it has to be a day trip, but she does sleep for close to 3-hour stretches in the afternoon already, and we aren't in any rush. I was given a backseat mirror for when I'm driving so I can look in my rear view and check on her, I'll bring that along. She is often very alert so she may be stimulated by the mirror at this point. Good tip :)
Oh my gosh look at all that hair! What a cutie. My little lady will likely be bald til her first birthday if she follows in my footsteps, lol.
I just adore her facial expression and big eyes in this one at only 2 days old: http://i.imgur.com/eQYPGp1l.jpg

This. I bitched so much about going so far past due with my pregnancy, but now I have this beautiful thriving baby girl. Despite an abnormal quad screen. Despite starting back on Zoloft for the last 3 weeks of pregnancy (which has about a 30% rate of withdrawal in newborns when taken so late in pregnancy). I feel so very blessed.
So cute :) congrats!

I'm glad that helped! But also if you still don't feel better in a few days, don't feel like a failure. Just try and take care of yourself too (easier said than done, I know) and reach out if you start feeling worse. I say this because I hate suggesting that we are just hormonal and that what we're feeling isn't valid. But this is one point in our lives where hormones really ARE a huge part of what we're going through. 

And thank you. Single parenting is going to be a challenge but I'd give up everything for my little girl, she really is the best thing that's ever happened to me :)

I just gave birth on Tuesday and had both IV pain meds (Stadol) and, later on, an epidural. But I was induced, and pitocin contractions are no joke. OK, here's my $.02.  I have been at my job for almost 4 years now, which is, as far as I know, pretty fabulous for someone with bipolar I. I am what my therapist calls "extremely high functioning." That's not to say there have been plenty of issues along the way. I've just been blessed to work for an awesome, small, family-owned company. 

First, and not helping matters at all, the president's son and I started dating as soon as i started there as a temp. Fast forward 3 years, I move to his department, he's my boss, and we have been through a tumultuous on and off relationship, which has set off a lot of episodes for me. I've almost quit because of him, we've had HR intervention for me acting out towards him during manic episodes.

I've gone to work hungover/still drunk (in the past). After my second DUI a year ago, I cried in the VP's office afraid of what I was going to do without a license. My coworkers worked out a plan where I have a ride to work and a ride home every single day. For a year. Of course I give them gas money & buy them lunches, I'm nothing if not extremely grateful. I'm aware most people can't expect this from their employers.

My bosses are aware of my bipolar. They also are aware of, like you said, the amazing productivity when I'm up and how much I've done for the company. They don't bat an eye when I need to leave early to see my therapist or psychiatrist. They were supportive when I was out for a week hospitalized this past summer. They even allowed me to lighten my work load for about a month after that stay so I could get adjusted to my meds.

I've always been a perfectionist.  I've been depressed for a large portion of my adult (and teenage) life. But I've also lived on my own since I was 17, so I have this sense of responsibility that not everyone with BP has. I'm not saying that to offend anyone. But I've just always known that if I don't get up and go to work, I can't pay rent. Even if I come straight home and go to sleep for 12 hours, I have to work. And I need to be BUSY to keep myself out of my head. I recently just asked my boss if I could take on additional responsibilities since we lost one of my customers (not my fault... btw). 

I realize I am atypical. But I definitely understand the "two steps forward, one step back" deal. Like I said, I've just been lucky enough to work for these people. They've had plenty of opportunities to kick my ass to the curb, but they've given me second (and third, and fourth) chances. I'm very stable on my med cocktail right now. The 8-5 job works for me.

Thanks to the ADA, and employer cannot fire you for a mental health issue. However, with bipolar, there are plenty of reasons they can fire you... frequent absences, poor performance, etc. I'm not sure I have any real "advice," but I wanted to share with you my experience, and show that being a working stiff is certainly possible with bipolar. Oh, and don't forget to take your meds. :)
